title: Period and frequency are reciprocals
ced_evidence: 3.5.A.2: "The period and frequency of a sinusoidal function are reciprocals."

title: Concavity of sinusoidal graphs
body: As input values increase, the graph of a sinusoidal function oscillates between concave down and concave up.
caution: Describe concavity as concave up or concave down. Do not use calculus-style wording such as "increasing at an increasing rate", which the scoring guidelines say requires calculus.
ced_evidence: 3.5.A.5: "the graphs of sinusoidal functions oscillate between concave down and concave up"

title: Converting frequency to the parameter b
caution: A frequency such as 200 cycles per second gives b = 2π·200. It is not the period, so do not set b equal to the frequency, and do not use 2π divided by the frequency.
ced_evidence: 3.5.A.2 "period and frequency ... are reciprocals" with 3.6.A.6 "a period of (1/b)2π units"; used in 3.7.A.1

title: Contextual domain for models and equations
body: A sinusoidal model of data is often useful only over its contextual domain, and a domain restriction implied by the context limits the number of solutions to a trigonometric equation or inequality.
ced_evidence: 3.7.A.5: "frequently only useful over their contextual domain"; 3.10.A.3: "domain restriction that can be implied from the context, which limits the number of solutions"

title: Building a sinusoidal model from data
body: Key values of a sinusoidal model are estimated from period, extreme values, and a matching input-output pair, or found with technology.

items.label: Period and frequency
items.meaning: Use the input-value interval between consecutive maxima or consecutive minima (3.7.A.1).

items.label: Amplitude and vertical shift
items.meaning: Use the maximum and minimum output values. The amplitude is half their difference and the midline is their average (3.7.A.2, 3.5.A.3, 3.5.A.4).

items.label: Phase shift
items.meaning: Compare an actual input-output pair with pairs produced by the model (3.7.A.3).

items.label: Technology
items.meaning: Estimate key values or use sinusoidal regression for a data set (3.7.A.4).

title: Secant, cosecant, and cotangent definitions
ced_evidence: 3.11.A.1–3.11.A.4: "the reciprocal of the cosine function"; "the reciprocal of the sine function"; "cot θ = cos θ / sin θ"
